summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on cipher-box PR #296, then fix a cascading series of CI E2E test failures that emerged after the PR was merged.
summary.outcome: All PR review comments were resolved across multiple rounds; CI E2E failures were traced to missing package builds, wrong __ZUSTAND_STORES exposure in production builds, and an async race condition — culminating in a full rewrite of conflict-detection tests to use a second browser session instead of direct API calls, eliminating all Zustand store access from E2E tests.

repo: The E2E tests run against `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web dev` (Vite dev server), NOT a production build — so VITE_* env vars must be set in the dev server environment, not in the build step

CI workflows (e2e.yml, deploy-staging.yml, e2e-desktop.yml) only built @cipherbox/crypto before web; the new packages (core, api-client, sdk-core, sdk) were never added and must be built in dependency order first
__ZUSTAND_STORES is gated behind import.meta.env.DEV in main.tsx, so it was never available in CI E2E runs

release-please uses the target branch name ('main') as the PR title suffix when multiple components are versioned together — pull-request-title-pattern with ${version} doesn't work for multi-component repos
The ensureFolderRegistered isLoaded guard added from a Copilot review comment broke uploads because SDK-created folders and root folders have valid keys but isLoaded is not set in all code paths
FolderTree.clear() zeros all stored key buffers, so registerFolder storing caller-owned buffers allows destroy() to zero the caller's memory — defensive copies are necessary
orval codegen generates wrong type for nullable Date fields (produces { [key: string]: unknown } | null instead of string | null) — regenerating produces the same incorrect output

code.finding: Dynamic import().then() for vault store caused race condition — __E2E was not set by the time conflict-detection beforeAll ran page.evaluate(). Static import fixes this.
webServer uses 'pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web dev' — dev server, not production build
ensureFolderRegistered guard on isLoaded was too strict — caused silent no-op registrations, breaking all upload mutations with 'Folder not loaded'
Test 3.7 used waitForFunction checking window.__ZUSTAND_STORES?.vault which never resolves in CI; replaced with waiting for file list UI element
fileKey not cleared if exception occurs before re-wrap try/catch — security leak; fixed with try/finally wrapping entire post-upload path
Rewrote to use a second browser context with the same wallet identity to naturally bump server sequence via UI upload, instead of direct API calls requiring accessToken/rootIpnsName

workflow: When PR is already merged, always create a new branch from latest main before making fixes — pushing to merged branch doesn't reach main
Check PR merge status before committing/pushing fixes (gh pr view --json mergedAt)
Expose minimal test helpers (window.__E2E with just the needed getters) rather than full Zustand store objects — but prefer UI-based approaches entirely when possible
Using a second browser session with the same wallet identity is cleaner than direct API calls for simulating multi-device conflicts in E2E tests
VITE_* env vars baked into production builds are useless when E2E uses dev server — env must be in the dev server process

friction: Repeatedly committed fixes to already-merged branches before checking merge status — happened 3+ times across the session

The __ZUSTAND_STORES approach went through multiple failed iterations (expose unconditionally → VITE_E2E flag → async import race → static import) before the correct diagnosis (dev server vs build) emerged
The ensureFolderRegistered isLoaded guard added from a reviewer comment immediately broke uploads in CI, requiring a follow-up PR
PR #296 was the root cause of multiple cascading failures (missing CI package builds, broken E2E test assumptions, wrong store exposure) that required 6+ follow-up PRs to resolve
CI runs on already-merged code made it hard to validate fixes quickly — each iteration required a new branch and PR
open_items: web3auth-helpers.ts still contains __ZUSTAND_STORES references — it's legacy/unused by wallet-based tests but was not cleaned up
The recycle-bin quota check was rewritten to use UI but the full test coverage of quota assertions was not verified in CI
The orval codegen issue with nullable Date fields (VaultResponseDtoInitializedAt) generates wrong types and was marked not applicable — upstream orval bug, no fix in place
Concurrent folder mutations (PR review Thread 2) was marked not applicable as an architectural concern — UI-level serialization was noted as the existing mitigation, follow-up improvement deferred
Test 3.7 (reload/session restore) is sensitive to Sapphire Devnet latency on CI — pre-existing flakiness acknowledged but not fundamentally addressed
